note: All rules RULE_DRAFT. Live screening requires RULE_APPROVED with an independent reviewer (not the author).

rules.condition: Status category must be Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or protected person. A study permit or work permit alone does not meet this criterion.
rules.evidence_span: be a Canadian citizen, a permanent resident or have protected person status
rules.author: Diya Giri

rules.condition: Must be a resident of British Columbia as defined by StudentAid BC.
rules.evidence_span: be a resident of British Columbia
rules.coverage_limit: StudentAid BC residency definition (linked page) not reviewed. Arrival in BC is not proof of residency. Always review_required until reviewed.
rules.author: Diya Giri

rules.condition: Eligible program at an eligible school, financial need, and satisfactory academic progress.
rules.evidence_span: be able to demonstrate financial need
exceptions: be enrolled in an eligible program of study at an eligible post-secondary school
make academic progress and achieve satisfactory scholastic standing in each period of post-secondary study
Delinquent or in default of previous student loans.
rules.coverage_limit: Not assessed by VERA. Always review_required; hand off to official StudentAid BC application. No funding amount output.
rules.author: Diya Giri

rules.condition: Status must be one of the BC NSP listed categories. Work permit holders qualify. Citizens qualify only if naturalized. Other listed categories are not modeled and route to review.
rules.evidence_span: You are eligible for the BC Newcomer Services Program (BC NSP) if you are a:
exceptions: temporary worker with a valid work permit
international post-secondary student on a study permit (if services are not offered at your educational institution)
provincial nominee awaiting a decision on your application for permanent residency
naturalized Canadian citizen
displaced Ukrainian (including immediate family members) with valid CUAET visas
refugee claimant (more support is available through the BC Safe Haven program).
rules.coverage_limit: Permanent residents are not a listed category; route PRs to NEW-03. Provider intake and availability remain external.
rules.author: Diya Giri

rules.condition: If the person is an international post-secondary student on a study permit, BC NSP applies only if their educational institution does not offer the service. Unknown availability stays unknown.
rules.evidence_span: international post-secondary student on a study permit (if services are not offered at your educational institution)
rules.coverage_limit: Do not infer institutional service availability from school identity.
rules.author: Diya Giri

rules.condition: Status must be in an IRCC settlement-eligible category. Ordinary study-permit or work-permit status alone is not a general route.
rules.evidence_span: You're eligible for our services if you're:
exceptions: a permanent resident (PR), including a resettled refugee
a successful permanent residence applicant (approved in principle)
a protected person who received a positive decision from the Immigration and Refugee Board (IRB)
a temporary resident (or their dependant) in certain employment programs, such as:
a person approved under certain pathways, such as:
a participant of Francophone Minority Communities Student Pilot (including their families)
rules.coverage_limit: Exception programs and pathways are listed as unchecked; any user in them gets review_required.
rules.author: Diya Giri

rules.condition: Economic-class PRs may access services for a limited period from the date they became a PR (6 years from April 1, 2026; 5 years for those becoming PR from April 1, 2027).
rules.evidence_span: starting April 1, 2026, you can access newcomer services for up to 6 years from the date you became a PR
exceptions: starting April 1, 2027, you can access the services for up to 5 years from the date you became a PR
rules.coverage_limit: Date calculator DISABLED. S4 transition wording ('These changes apply to all economic class PRs, including people who became PRs before April 1, 2026.') must be reconciled with Examples 1-3 and month-end endpoints before enabling. Until approved, return review_required and link official guidance.
rules.author: Diya Giri

rules.condition: No time limit applies to non-economic PRs, resettled refugees, protected persons, and temporary residents approved under certain programs or pathways.
rules.evidence_span: There's no time limit to access newcomer services if you're
exceptions: a PR approved through a non-economic PR program
a resettled refugee
a protected person, or
a temporary resident approved under certain programs or pathways
rules.author: Diya Giri
